Reliability and item analysis table

Source: R/reliability.R
apa_reliability.Rd

Makes an APA-style table of the reliability of one or more scales: for each item, its mean, standard deviation, corrected item-total correlation, and Cronbach's \(\alpha\) if the item were deleted, followed for each scale by the scale score's mean and standard deviation, Cronbach's \(\alpha\) with its confidence interval, McDonald's \(\omega_{\text{total}}\), and the mean inter-item correlation.

Usage

apa_reliability(
  data,
  scales = NULL,
  reverse = NULL,
  item_range = NULL,
  level = c("items", "scales"),
  omega = TRUE,
  ci = 0.95,
  score = c("mean", "sum"),
  flag = FALSE,
  min_item_total = 0.3,
  format_variable_names = TRUE,
  digits = 2
)

Arguments

data

data frame of item responses

scales

named list of character vectors of item names, one for each scale (e.g., list(Agreeableness = c("A1", "A2", "A3"))). If NULL (default), all columns of data form one scale.

reverse

names of items to reverse-score before the analysis. Items are reversed within their scale's range of responses (item_range), and they are marked "(R)" in the table.

item_range

lowest and highest possible responses, used to reverse items. If NULL (default), the lowest and highest responses observed in each scale are used.

level

"items" (default) for item rows followed by each scale's statistics, or "scales" for one row per scale.

omega

if TRUE (default), McDonald's \(\omega_{\text{total}}\) is shown

ci

confidence level of the interval of \(\alpha\)

score

"mean" (default) or "sum": how scale scores are computed

flag

if TRUE, item-total correlations below min_item_total and \(\alpha\)-if-deleted values above the scale's \(\alpha\) are bolded

min_item_total

cutoff for flagging item-total correlations

format_variable_names

if TRUE (default), item and scale names are lightly formatted: underscores become spaces, and the first letter is capitalized (item codes such as "A1" stay intact). Set to FALSE to keep names exactly as they are.

digits

number of decimal places

Value

apa7_tbl (tibble)

Details

The corrected item-total correlation (r~it~) is the item's correlation with the sum of the other items in its scale. Items with low values (often, below .30) discriminate poorly. \(\alpha\) if deleted is the scale's \(\alpha\) without the item; values above the scale's \(\alpha\) mean that the item lowers reliability.

Cronbach's \(\alpha\), the item statistics, and the mean inter-item correlation come from psych::alpha(). The confidence interval of \(\alpha\) is Feldt's. \(\omega_{\text{total}}\) is computed from a one-factor model (psych::fa(), minimum residual): \((\sum\lambda)^2 / ((\sum\lambda)^2 + \sum\psi)\).

Each scale uses the respondents who answered all of its items, and the note gives their number. Scale scores are the means of the items (or their sums, with score = "sum").

When all items of a scale are scored 0 and 1 (e.g., incorrect and correct answers), M is the item's difficulty (the proportion of 1s), r~it~ is the corrected point-biserial correlation, and \(\alpha\) equals KR-20. The note says so.

Examples

d <- psych::bfi
apa_reliability(
  d,
  scales = list(
    Agreeableness = paste0("A", 1:5),
    Conscientiousness = paste0("C", 1:5)
  ),
  reverse = c("A1", "C4", "C5"),
  item_range = c(1, 6)
)
#> # A tibble: 20 × 5
#>    Item                  `*M*`            `*SD*` `*r*~it~` `&alpha; if deleted`
#>    <chr>                 <chr>            <chr>  <chr>     <chr>               
#>  1 Agreeableness         ""               ""     ""        ""                  
#>  2  A1 (R)               "4.59"           "1.40" ".31"     ".72"               
#>  3  A2                   "4.80"           "1.18" ".56"     ".62"               
#>  4  A3                   "4.60"           "1.30" ".59"     ".60"               
#>  5  A4                   "4.68"           "1.49" ".39"     ".69"               
#>  6  A5                   "4.55"           "1.26" ".49"     ".64"               
#>  7  Scale mean (*k* = 5) "4.64"           "0.90" ""        ""                  
#>  8  &alpha; [95% CI]     ".70 [.69, .72]" ""     ""        ""                  
#>  9  *&omega;*~total~     ".72"            ""     ""        ""                  
#> 10  Mean inter-item *r*  ".33"            ""     ""        ""                  
#> 11 Conscientiousness     ""               ""     ""        ""                  
#> 12  C1                   "4.51"           "1.24" ".46"     ".70"               
#> 13  C2                   "4.36"           "1.32" ".51"     ".68"               
#> 14  C3                   "4.30"           "1.29" ".47"     ".69"               
#> 15  C4 (R)               "4.45"           "1.37" ".56"     ".66"               
#> 16  C5 (R)               "3.69"           "1.63" ".48"     ".69"               
#> 17  Scale mean (*k* = 5) "4.26"           "0.95" ""        ""                  
#> 18  &alpha; [95% CI]     ".73 [.71, .75]" ""     ""        ""                  
#> 19  *&omega;*~total~     ".73"            ""     ""        ""                  
#> 20  Mean inter-item *r*  ".35"            ""     ""        ""                  

# One row per scale
apa_reliability(
  d,
  scales = list(
    Agreeableness = paste0("A", 1:5),
    Conscientiousness = paste0("C", 1:5)
  ),
  reverse = c("A1", "C4", "C5"),
  item_range = c(1, 6),
  level = "scales"
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 8
#>   Scale      `*k*` `*M*` `*SD*` `&alpha;` `95% CI` `*&omega;*~total~` `Mean *r*`
#>   <chr>      <chr> <chr> <chr>  <chr>     <chr>    <chr>              <chr>     
#> 1 Agreeable… 5     4.64  0.90   .70       [.69, .… .72                .33       
#> 2 Conscient… 5     4.26  0.95   .73       [.71, .… .73                .35
